cross_verification.note_en: 'Headshot / Profile Photo' (400x400px+, solid-colour background, no head-height spec) is not a government-regulated document type in the way Passport/Visa/ID are — it reads as a generic professional/social profile photo (e.g. LinkedIn, resume, corporate directory), for which the U.S. federal government has no single binding specification. The nearest official U.S. analogues were checked directly: (1) travel.state.gov passport/visa digital photos require a SQUARE image between 600x600 and 1200x1200 pixels with a white/off-white background (travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/photos/digital-image-requirements.html) — a 400x400px image would fail this as too small; (2) CBP Global Entry / Trusted Traveler photos follow the same 2x2in/51x51mm passport-style spec (cbp.gov/travel/trusted-traveler-programs/global-entry). Neither matches the DB's 400x400px 'solid colour' headshot spec, confirming this slug is not the same product as us-passport/us-visa (already researched separately) and has no discoverable official government source of its own. Left entirely unverified rather than borrowing the passport/visa numbers, which would misattribute them to the wrong document type.
